title: Linear-Time Principal Component Analysis via Balanced Search-Based Matrix Decomposition in C
topic: Principal Component Analysis with Linear-Time Matrix Decompositions
author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a cornerstone of high-dimensional data reduction, yet classical matrix decompositions incur quadratic or cubic costs. We present a C implementation that achieves linear-time extraction of the dominant eigenvector by representing the data matrix as a height-balanced binary search tree over non-zero entries. The tree supports $O(log N)$ search and $O(log N)$ insertion, while each matrix-vector multiplication reduces to a linear scan over the tree's leaves, yielding $O(n)$ time per iteration under constant sparsity. We formally prove that the tree maintains strict height-balance and key-order invariants, guaranteeing the asymptotic bounds. Static Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) inspection confirms a structural complexity of 188 source lines and a single function block, with a worst-case search cost of $O(log N)$. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261006_032154_quantum_1-pca_with_pauli_measu}.
